text: Which series of models is OpenAI best known for developing?
options: The GPT series of large language models
The Claude series of large language models
The Gemini series of large language models
The Llama series of large language models
answer: The GPT series of large language models
explanation: GPT stands for generative pre-trained transformer, and the name has been carried through the whole line since the original 2018 model. The other three series on this list belong to Anthropic, Google and Meta, which is a quick way to rule three options out and check the fourth.
answerAliases: generative pre-trained transformer (GPT) series of large language models

text: Anthropic and OpenAI are both headquartered in the same American city. Which city?
explanation: Both are public benefit corporations registered and based in San Francisco, and both were founded by people who had just left the same organisation. The overlap in people, funding and hiring is the single largest structural fact about the frontier lab industry.

text: Which French AI company, founded in 2023 and based in Paris, is known for open weight language models?
explanation: Mistral released the Mixtral mixture of experts model under an Apache licence, which was the first genuinely competitive open weight model from a European lab. The valuation above 14 billion dollars makes it the most valuable European AI company.

text: Which Hangzhou based AI company develops open weight models and is owned and funded by a hedge fund?
explanation: DeepSeek is funded by High-Flyer, which is unusual, since it means the research is not being driven by outside investors looking for a return. Their reasoning models made strong performance on math and code benchmarks at unusually low cost, and the models were released with open weights.
answerAliases: Hangzhou DeepSeek Artificial Intelligence Basic Technology Research Co., Ltd.

text: Which Seattle based non-profit research institute was founded in 2014 by Microsoft co-founder Paul Allen?
explanation: Ai2, as it styles itself, was built to do open research rather than to ship products, and the distinction matters. The Allen Institute for Brain Science is a separate organisation in Seattle that studies neural tissue, and the two are easy to mix up because they share a name and a benefactor.

source.title: Allen Institute for AI
source.label: Allen Institute for AI on Wikipedia

text: Which lab was founded in 2010, acquired by Google in 2014, and later merged with Google Brain in 2023?
explanation: DeepMind was founded in London and became the company behind AlphaGo, AlphaFold and Gemini. Google paid a reported 400 million pounds for it, and the merge with Google Brain in April 2023 is what created the awkward situation of two research groups with the same name inside one company.

text: Which Toronto based company focuses on large language models for regulated industries such as banking and healthcare?
explanation: Aidan Gomez, Ivan Zhang and Nick Frosst founded Cohere in 2019, and Gomez was also the first author of the transformer paper that everything modern is built on. The pitch is deployment inside regulated companies rather than a consumer chatbot, which is a slower business with far fewer users.

text: In which year did Google merge DeepMind with its Google Brain division to form Google DeepMind?
explanation: Google had already bought DeepMind in 2014, and for nine years it and Google Brain ran as separate organisations with overlapping goals. The 2023 merge left one research lab with a duplicated name inside it, which is a fairly ordinary outcome of acquisitions and an unusually visible one here.

text: Which lab develops the Claude family of AI models?
explanation: Claude is the flagship product of Anthropic, the public benefit corporation founded in January 2021 by former OpenAI members including Dario and Daniela Amodei with an explicit AI safety mission. OpenAI is the tempting wrong answer because the Amodeis came from there, but OpenAI builds the GPT series, not Claude.

text: Which lab develops the Gemini family of AI models?
explanation: Google DeepMind is responsible for the proprietary Gemini family alongside the open-weight Gemma models, after Google merged DeepMind with the Google Brain division in April 2023. OpenAI is the closest distractor since GPT and Gemini compete head to head, but GPT belongs to OpenAI.

text: Which lab develops the Llama family of AI models?
explanation: Meta AI is the research division behind the Llama models, which Meta released with open weights and built its Meta AI assistant on. Mistral AI is the natural confusion because the Paris lab also publishes open-weight models, but its family is Mistral and Mixtral, not Llama.

text: Which former OpenAI chief scientist co-founded Safe Superintelligence Inc.?
explanation: Ilya Sutskever founded SSI with Daniel Gross and Daniel Levy after leaving OpenAI in May 2024, with a mission focused on building safe superintelligence. Sam Altman is the closest distractor as the OpenAI CEO whose brief removal preceded Sutskever's exit, but Altman stayed and Sutskever left to start SSI.

text: Which former OpenAI chief technology officer founded Thinking Machines Lab in 2025?
explanation: Mira Murati, OpenAI's former chief technology officer, founded Thinking Machines Lab in February 2025 as a San Francisco public benefit corporation. Ilya Sutskever is the tempting alternative because he also left OpenAI to found a lab, but his lab is SSI, founded a year earlier.

text: What does World Labs, the startup founded by Fei-Fei Li, build?
options: AI accelerator chips for data centers
explanation: World Labs came out of stealth in September 2024 with $230 million in funding to build large world models that perceive and interact with the 3D world, aimed at artists, designers and game studios. Protein folding is DeepMind's AlphaFold territory, while Li's bet is that spatial intelligence is the frontier after language.

text: Which AI lab was created by Google LaMDA developers Noam Shazeer and Daniel De Freitas?
explanation: Shazeer and De Freitas built LaMDA at Google, then left to found Character.ai, whose beta opened in September 2022 with customizable characters that users define and publish. Inflection AI is the closest distractor because it is also a chatbot lab, but its product was Pi and its founders came from DeepMind, not LaMDA.

text: In August 2026, Google handed day-to-day leadership of Google DeepMind to a 13-year veteran of the lab, who took the new title of senior vice-president. Which veteran?
explanation: Google's own memo announced that Koray Kavukcuoglu would step up as SVP of Google DeepMind, while Demis Hassabis gave up day-to-day operations to become chair of GDM and chief scientist of Alphabet. Kavukcuoglu had already been the lab's CTO and Google's chief AI architect. Oriol Vinyals is the tempting wrong answer because he was a DeepMind research VP at the time, but he left Google days later to co-found Discovery Loop.

source.label: Sundar Pichai and Demis Hassabis on the Google DeepMind leadership change

text: In August 2026, Jeff Dean, Sanjay Ghemawat, Oriol Vinyals and Quoc Le left Google together to found a new research lab. Which lab?
explanation: Discovery Loop is a Palo Alto public benefit corporation whose stated goal is automating the propose-run-evaluate loop of scientific research, starting with machine learning itself. Google stayed in as a founding investor and cloud partner, so losing four researchers turned into an equity position. Ineffable Intelligence is the tempting wrong answer because it is the other ex-DeepMind lab that raised over a billion dollars, but David Silver founded that one months earlier.

text: In the six days from June 18 to June 24, 2026, four senior Google DeepMind researchers said or were reported to be leaving for rival labs, and three of the four headed for the same company. Which company?
explanation: John Jumper, who shared the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for AlphaFold, announced first, and Gemini contributors Jonas Adler and Alexander Pritzel followed within days. Gemini co-lead Noam Shazeer was the only one of the four who chose OpenAI, less than two years after Google paid billions to bring him back from Character.AI. Both OpenAI and Anthropic were close to going public, which is what made pre-IPO equity worth swapping a stable job for.

source.label: TechCrunch on the June 2026 Google departures

text: In July 2026, Thinking Machines Lab co-founder Lilian Weng announced she was stepping down citing her health, then rejoined which lab two days later?
explanation: Weng ran OpenAI's safety organisation before leaving in November 2024 to co-found Thinking Machines with Mira Murati, and she went back to lead a team supporting recursive self-improvement research. Murati stayed at her own lab, which is why the return looked awkward two days after the resignation note. Anthropic is the tempting wrong answer because it is Thinking Machines' most direct competitor.

text: In August 2026, Nvidia's vice president of AI research left the company after eight years to found a Toronto startup building world models so robots can train inside simulation. Which researcher was that?
explanation: Fidler ran Nvidia's Toronto spatial intelligence lab and was part of the team behind its Cosmos world model before announcing her departure. Her co-founders are Zan Gojcic, the former Nvidia research director in Zurich who is now CTO, and Huan Ling, her former doctoral student who is chief scientist. David Silver is the tempting wrong answer because he is the other ex-DeepMind founder with a billion-dollar lab, but his company is Ineffable Intelligence.

source.label: The Recursive on Veeda AI's founding round

text: In August 2026, the researcher who led Alibaba's Qwen model family founded a new AI lab in Shanghai. Which lab did he start?
explanation: Junyang Lin left Alibaba in March 2026 with a post reading 'Bye my beloved Qwen', then named his new Shanghai lab after pragmatics, the study of meaning in context, which is roughly what an agent has to do. Zhipu AI is the tempting wrong answer because it is one of the best-known Chinese labs shipping open-weight models, but it has nothing to do with Lin. The Shanghai AI Laboratory is a real institute too, but a state-backed research body rather than a founder-led startup.

source.label: RuntimeWire on Junyang Lin's Pragmatik Labs

text: In July 2026, Richard Sutton and his former student Khurram Javed left John Carmack's Keen Technologies to found a new lab in Toronto. What did they call it?
explanation: Sutton, who shared the 2024 Turing Award for founding modern reinforcement learning, started Oak Lab to build agents that keep learning after deployment. His stated target is an agent with a trillion parameters that learns and plans in real time on about 20 watts, roughly human-brain power. Skyfall AI is the tempting wrong answer because it launched from Toronto in the same month, but it came from the Maluuba founders.

source.label: The Decoder on Oak Lab's launch

text: In August 2026, a Princeton-rooted research lab for scientific computing came out of stealth with a $10.6 million round led by Dimension. Which of its three founders had previously co-founded the Wolfram Physics Project?
explanation: Gorard is an applied mathematician who co-founded the Wolfram Physics Project with Stephen Wolfram and now runs Lanyon as CEO. His co-founders are Ammar Hakim, the computational physicist who is CTO, and James Juno, the plasma physicist. Ammar Hakim is the tempting wrong answer because he is the better-known senior scientist of the pair, but the Wolfram connection is Gorard's.

source.label: Physical AI News on Lanyon AI's founding team

text: In August 2026, which US chipmaker unveiled its own long-horizon research lab, headquartered in Boise, Idaho?
explanation: Micron Research Labs is a planned ten billion dollar research campus in Boise that will host hundreds of researchers working on memory and AI, with construction slated to begin in 2027. Nvidia is the tempting wrong answer because it is by far the largest AI chip company, but this is the American memory maker building for its own next decade alongside its two new Boise fabs.

source.label: Engineering News-Record on Micron Research Labs

text: In July 2026, the LinkedIn co-founder Reid Hoffman and the Zynga founder Mark Pincus were reported to be backing a new research lab focused on computer-use models. Which lab?
explanation: Prentis launched in April 2026 with serial entrepreneur Ritankar Das as CEO and trains models inside real office workflows rather than on web-scale text. Manas AI is the tempting wrong answer because it is Hoffman's own drug-discovery startup, which he went into founder mode on after leaving Microsoft's board. Inflection AI is the other lab he co-founded, back in 2022.
